name: il-s42-720h-crossing-midweek
summary: An Illinois day laborer in Joliet at $17.00/h, billed at $24.00/h, has already worked 700 hours (42,000 minutes) at the same client in the past 12 months (105 days of 6 h 40 m from November 2, 2025). In the week of Monday October 12, 2026 the worker works 8 hours a day, 7:00 to 15:00. The counter after each day: Monday 42,480, Tuesday 42,960; on Wednesday it reaches 43,200 minutes (720 hours) at 11:00, so the minute from 11:00 is the first over 720 hours in the 12 months from October 15, 2025 (820 ILCS 175/42(a)). Hours after the crossing this week: 4 h on Wednesday + 8 h + 8 h = 20 h. The equal-pay rate needs the client's comparator data, so pay is unchanged — 40 h × $17.00 = $680.00; bill 40 h × $24.00 = $960.00 — and the result records an obligation (crossed on October 14 at 11:00, client data due before the next pay period: 56 Ill. Adm. Code 260.505(b)) with warnings that equal pay now applies and that 20 h were paid at the placement rate.

equalPayRules.citation: 820 ILCS 175/42(a) (P.A. 103-1030, eff. 2024-08-09) — equal pay and benefits (or their hourly cash value, § 42(b)) after more than 720 hours at the same third party client within a 12-month period, counting work on or after April 1, 2024; § 42(a)(2)(B), (c): more than 4,160 hours within a 48-month period; 56 Ill. Adm. Code 260.445, 260.505(b) — the client's data is due before the next pay period begins. The 600-hour heads-up is Granite's (SPEC §9), not law.

regularRateRules.citation: 29 U.S.C. § 207(e)(6) — a premium rate for work on holidays, Saturdays, Sundays or regular days of rest of not less than one and one-half times the rate for like work on other days stays out of the regular rate; a smaller premium counts in it (29 C.F.R. § 778.203); California follows (DLSE Enforcement Manual 49.1.2.4)

payLines.explain: Regular: 40h 00m (2400 min) × $17.00/h = 68000¢ exactly → $680.00. Rule straight_time: hours up to the 40h 00m weekly threshold in the workweek starting 2026-10-12.

billLines.explain: Billed regular: 40h 00m (2400 min) × $24.00/h = 96000¢ exactly → $960.00. Bill rate from the rate card.

warnings.message: Worker One passed 720 hours of work at Client X on 2026-10-14 at 11:00 (the 12 months from 2025-10-15): from then on the Illinois equal-pay rule applies: at least the pay of the client's comparable direct hires, with equal benefits or their hourly cash value (820 ILCS 175/42). Get the client's pay, seniority and benefits data before the next pay period begins (56 Ill. Adm. Code 260.505(b)), then enter the equal-pay rate.

Worker One, workweek starting 2026-10-12: 20h 00m worked at Client X after passing 720 hours there are paid at the placement rate; the equal-pay rate and benefits (or their hourly cash value) are not on file, so back pay may be due once they are (820 ILCS 175/42).
